acceptance_tests: Run ERC on the corrected schematic and verify zero unresolved errors; review every warning.
Inspect the schematic/netlist and verify USB Type-C input, regulated 3.3 V, common ground, ESP32 power, TMP102 power, SDA, SCL, and ADD0 connectivity.
Verify SDA connects TMP102 SDA to ESP32 GPIO21 and SCL connects TMP102 SCL to ESP32 GPIO22 at 3.3 V logic levels.
Verify USB D+ and D- are either fully implemented for a supported data function or explicitly unused.
Run DRC on the completed two-layer layout and verify zero unresolved errors; review every warning.
Measure the powered board's 3.3 V rail and verify correct operation from nominal 5 V USB Type-C input.
Read the TMP102 from the ESP32 over I2C and confirm a plausible, stable temperature value.
Check that the finished outline is no larger than 110 mm by 65 mm and passes generic_two_layer manufacturing checks.
constraints: Propose requirements only; do not modify the project or produce circuit design.
Return the design to schematic engineering before layout because the current USB Micro-B connector conflicts with the USB-C requirement.
Complete and validate sensor power, I2C connectivity, and USB-C power connectivity before PCB layout.
Do not approve release while ERC or DRC errors remain unresolved.

power.input: USB Type-C, nominal 5 V sink input

requirements.statement: The PCB shall accept nominal 5 V power through a USB Type-C receptacle configured as a power sink.

requirements.source: ESP32-WROOM-32 and TMP102 logic supply requirement; current net list omits TMP102 VCC.
requirements.statement: The PCB shall provide a regulated 3.3 V logic rail to the ESP32 module and TMP102 sensor.

requirements.source: Current nets show TMP102 VCC absent and TMP102 ADD0 connected to GND.
requirements.statement: All required ESP32 and TMP102 supply and ground pins shall have intentional power-net connections, including TMP102 VCC and GND.

requirements.source: Project request conflicts with current J1 USB_B_Micro.
requirements.statement: The external power connector shall be USB Type-C; the listed USB Micro-B connector shall not remain in the release design.

requirements.source: Project request and provided ESP32/TMP102 pin table.
requirements.statement: The TMP102 shall communicate with the ESP32 over one 3.3 V I2C bus using GPIO21 as SDA and GPIO22 as SCL.

requirements.source: TMP102 address selection requirement; current net list connects U2.5 ADD0 to GND.
requirements.statement: The TMP102 ADD0 pin shall be intentionally strapped to a valid logic level so its I2C address is deterministic and documented.

requirements.source: Current design lists USB_D+ and USB_D- connections although the project requests USB-C power.
requirements.statement: USB D+ and D- shall either be intentionally connected end-to-end for a supported USB data function or explicitly marked unused; they shall not be unintentionally floating or partially connected.
The finished board outline shall not exceed the current 110 mm width by 65 mm height envelope.
The PCB shall use a two-layer stackup compatible with the generic_two_layer manufacturer profile.
Release ERC shall report zero unresolved errors; every remaining warning shall be reviewed and explicitly accepted with rationale or eliminated.
Release DRC shall report zero unresolved errors; every remaining warning shall be reviewed and explicitly accepted with rationale or eliminated.

requirements.source: Current net list has incomplete power and I2C connectivity.
requirements.statement: Connectivity inspection shall confirm the 5 V input path, regulated 3.3 V rail, common ground, ESP32 supply, TMP102 supply, and both I2C signals are complete with no unintended opens or shorts.

requirements.source: Project goal: ESP32 temperature-monitoring PCB with an I2C sensor.
requirements.statement: Powered functional validation shall demonstrate ESP32 communication with the TMP102 and acquisition of a plausible temperature reading over I2C.
Manufacturing review shall pass the generic_two_layer profile checks for board outline, layer count, clearances, routing, and fabrication readiness.
